prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: One critic who has examined them closely describes the painter's use of gold as ______.

worlds.passage: Many of the portraits a painter made in the last decade of her career include areas of gold leaf, and those late canvases are now her most studied. The gold first appears in three portraits she delivered in the winter of 1960, when a dock strike had halted shipments of yellow pigment. X-rays show each background half-painted in ochre and then covered with uneven scraps of leaf of the kind framers throw away, laid on so fast that brush hairs are trapped beneath them; the sitters, old friends, hung the pictures in their front rooms. One critic who has examined them closely describes the painter's use of gold as ______.
worlds.explanation: Gold appears when a strike cut off her pigment, laid over half-finished backgrounds in hasty scraps, so its use was "improvised." "Ingrained" fails because it first appears in 1960; "incidental" fails because it covers whole backgrounds; "ironic" fails because the sitters, her friends, displayed the pictures proudly.

ingrained.why: a practice that begins in 1960 is not a long-fixed habit

incidental.why: gold covering the backgrounds is not a minor touch

ironic.quote: hung the pictures in their front rooms
ironic.why: friends displaying their portraits did not read them as mockery

worlds.passage: Many of the portraits a painter made in the last decade of her career include areas of gold leaf, and those late canvases are now her most studied. She learned gilding at eight in her father's icon workshop, and X-rays of her student pictures show gold laid behind the figures before a single stroke of paint. The late portraits were built the same way, with the leaf going down first across each background; the sitters, old friends, hung the pictures in their front rooms. One critic who has examined them closely describes the painter's use of gold as ______.
worlds.explanation: A practice learned at eight and repeated in the same order from her student work to her last portraits is "ingrained." "Improvised" fails because the gold went down first, before any paint; "incidental" fails because it spans each background; "ironic" fails because the sitters, her friends, displayed the pictures proudly.

improvised.quote: before a single stroke of paint
improvised.why: gold laid first, by long routine, was not a makeshift

incidental.why: the gold is a major element

ironic.quote: hung the pictures in their front rooms
ironic.why: the sitters did not take the gold as mockery

worlds.passage: Many of the portraits a painter made in the last decade of her career include areas of gold leaf, and those late canvases are now her most studied. The gold first appears in 1960, and her sketchbooks plan each placement: a glint on a cufflink, the rim of a teacup, a wedding ring. None of these can be made out from across a room, where the faces and hands, painted with great tenderness, hold the eye; the sitters, old friends, hung the pictures in their front rooms. One critic who has examined them closely describes the painter's use of gold as ______.
worlds.explanation: Planned glints too small to see from across a room, while the faces hold the eye, make the gold "incidental." "Improvised" fails because her sketchbooks plan each placement; "ingrained" fails because it first appears in 1960; "ironic" fails because the faces are painted with tenderness and the sitters displayed the pictures proudly.

improvised.why: planned in advance, not a makeshift

ingrained.why: a late addition is not a deep-rooted habit

ironic.why: tender treatment of the sitters is not mockery

worlds.passage: Many of the portraits a painter made in the last decade of her career include areas of gold leaf, and those late canvases are now her most studied. The gold first appears in 1960, in portraits of three bankers who had refused her a loan in her lean years, and her sketchbooks show her enlarging it with each study. In the finished canvases the gilded wall swells until the man before it, painted small and pinched, seems to shrink into the riches he guarded; none of the three would hang his picture. One critic who has examined them closely describes the painter's use of gold as ______.
worlds.explanation: The bankers who refused her shrink into the riches they guarded, the gold turned against them, so its use is "ironic." "Improvised" fails because her sketchbooks show it enlarged study by study; "ingrained" fails because it first appears in 1960; "incidental" fails because the gilded wall swells to dominate each canvas.

improvised.why: worked out over studies, not a makeshift

ingrained.why: a late adoption is not a long-fixed habit

incidental.why: gold that dominates the canvas is not minor
